overview: Cholera is a severe diarrheal disease that can be fatal within hours if not treated. It is an acute diarrheal infection caused by consuming food or water contaminated with the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. Access to safe water, basic sanitation and hygiene is essential to prevent cholera.
symptoms: No symptoms, but can spread the bacteria through faeces
transmission: Consuming food or water contaminated with Vibrio cholerae
Direct contact with an infected person's faeces
risk_factors: Climate events like cyclones, floods or drought
Lack of investment in maintaining and improving WASH services and infrastructure
key_facts: 535 321 cases and 4007 deaths were reported to WHO from 45 countries in 2023
Cholera can be fatal within hours if not treated
The case fatality rate in treatment centres should remain below 1%
